Below all other objects.

One step down.

`count` copies along `offset` (x, y) from one copy to the next. Or give `distance` and

`columns` x `rows` places, `column_spacing` and `row_spacing` apart. The grid can be turned

`count` copies about `center`, `angle` apart. The default angle spreads the copies
and the original evenly over a full turn.

resize.description: Each copy is this many times larger than the one before (default 1).

retain.description: Keep the original (default true). If not, the original goes and the array fills its place too.

rotate.description: Each copy is turned this much more than the one before, in radians, about its own center.

Attributes.description: Graphic attributes. A missing field uses the class attribute.

ClassId.description: An ID: a UUID text such as 0190f1c2-7a3b-7c1d-8e2f-123456789abc.

Comment.description: One message in the thread of an issue.

edited.description: When the text was edited last (milliseconds since 1970).

id.description: The ID. A nil ID in a command means "make a new one".

CommentId.description: An ID: a UUID text such as 0190f1c2-7a3b-7c1d-8e2f-123456789abc.

EdgeId.description: The id of a edge in its surface model.

Edit.description:
One edit of a surface model. In a command: `{"op": "edit_surface", "id": ..., "edit":
{"action": "add_edges", "edges": [[[0, 0, 0], [1000, 0, 0]]]}}`.

oneOf.description:
Draws straight edges, each `[[x, y, z], [x, y, z]]` in the local coordinates of the model
(mm). Ends weld to vertices and edges, crossings split, and faces are made and split.
Erases edges: coplanar faces on both sides merge, other faces of the edges go.
Erases faces only; their edges stay.
Turns faces over: front and back change places.

Paint (MOD-05): puts a material on the front, the back or both sides of faces, or clears
it (`material` null). `material` is the id of a material resource of the document (its
text form); it is stored in the attribute `material` (front) or `back_material` (back) of
the face. Faces turned over swap the two.

Draws a chain of straight edges through the points (a closed one joins the last point to
the first) and keeps them as one curve (a circle or an arc, MOD-08), so that the pieces
stay one curve when other edges cut them. Welds, splits and faces work as in `AddEdges`.
When one of the pieces is in a curve already, the edges are drawn and no new curve is made.

Pushes or pulls a face along its normal by `distance` mm (positive is toward the front,
negative toward the back). See the module `pushpull` for the cases. The face keeps its id
and ends as the cap.

Intersect Faces (MOD-08): makes edges where faces in other planes cross, so that both
faces are split there, and splits edges where they pass through a face. `model`: all faces
and edges of the model. `selection`: where the given `faces` cross anything and where the
given `edges` pass through a face. Faces in one plane that overlap are not handled (they
are a problem of the model). See the module `intersect`.

Move, Rotate and Scale of geometry (MOD-05): moves the given `vertices`, all vertices of the
given `faces` and the ends of the given `edges` by an affine map. `matrix` has 12 numbers,
the three columns of the 3x3 part and then the translation (the layout of
`glam::DAffine3::to_cols_array`), in the local coordinates of the model. Every face that
has a moved vertex is refitted to a plane; a face that is no longer flat is folded into
triangles along new soft and smooth edges. See the module `transform`.

Copy of faces and edges in the same model (Move with Ctrl, `5x`): `count` copies, the
first placed by `matrix`, the next by the matrix applied twice, three times and so on
(a row of copies at the same step; a rotation turns each copy further). The copies have new
ids and weld to the geometry they land on. See the module `transform`.

Hide and Unhide (MOD-05): sets (`hidden: true`) or clears the attribute `hidden` of the
given faces and edges. Views, picking and the inference leave hidden items out unless
Hidden Geometry shows them. Nothing else changes: a hidden edge does not merge faces.

Offset (MOD-08): draws a copy of every loop of the face `distance` mm inside the face
(`outward` false, the default) or outside it, in the plane of the face, with miter
corners. The face splits along the new loops; a curve gives a curve. `distance` must be
larger than the length tolerance. See the module `offset`.

Soft and smooth edges (MOD-08): sets (`true`) or clears (`false`) the flags of the edges;
a flag that is not given stays as it is. A soft edge is not drawn, picked or inferred; the
faces on the sides of a smooth edge shade as one surface. Hidden is `set_hidden`. See the
module `style`.

Soften Edges (MOD-08): each of the edges between two faces at an angle below `angle`
degrees (0 to 180) becomes soft (and smooth with `smooth`); the others lose both flags.
Edges between coplanar faces are softened only with `coplanar`.

Follow Me (MOD-08): sweeps the face `face` (the profile) along the chain of edges `path`
(open: a solid with the profile and a new face as caps; closed: a ring without caps). The
new faces get the paint of the profile; a curve of the path or of the profile gives soft
and smooth edges. See the module `followme`.

FaceId.description: The id of a face in its surface model.

FileLink.description:
A link to the original file of an import, instead of the summaries of its entities (see the
module docs). It is a hint: the file may be gone or changed, and the hash tells.

bytes.description: The size of the file in bytes.

path.description: The absolute path of the file when it was imported.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the file as 64 lower-case hexadecimal digits.

Georeference.description: Where the drawing sits on the earth: CRS and origin.

HardscapePatch.description: Hardscape settings to change. Missing fields stay.

ImageResource.description: A picture: {sha256, format (png|jpeg), width, height, data (base64 of the file), thumb (base64 PNG), source?}. Use plant_style.set_picture to make one from a file.

oneOf.description: All faces and edges of the model.
The given faces and edges against the whole model.

id.description: The ID. A nil ID in a command means "make a new one".

modified.description: Milliseconds since 1970 (UTC). Every change sets it.

objects.description: The objects that the issue is about.

origin.description: Who made it: a person in the app, an agent, a script or another user.

point.description: The model point (x, y, z in mm) that the issue is about, for the pin.

priority.description: The priority, free text. The app offers `low`, `normal`, `high` and `critical`.

type.description:
The type, free text. The app offers `issue`, `error`, `warning`, `request`, `clash` and
`remark`.

IssueId.description: An ID: a UUID text such as 0190f1c2-7a3b-7c1d-8e2f-123456789abc.

IssuePatch.description:
The fields of an issue that `ModifyIssue` can change. A field that is left out stays. For
`assignee` and `due`, an empty text clears the field.

LandscapePatch.description: Landscape area settings to change. Missing fields stay.

LayerId.description: An ID: a UUID text such as 0190f1c2-7a3b-7c1d-8e2f-123456789abc.

LayerSource.description: The source of an imported layer.

drawing.description: The drawing (lineage), as in `ImportTag::drawing`. Layers are matched on it.

dxf_layer.description:
The name of the DXF layer, when the layer maps one. Empty for a layer that holds the
whole file.

link.description:
The original file, when the import kept no summaries of the entities because the drawing
has too many (`base: "link"`). An update reads the old file from here.

revision.description: The revision that was imported last.

shift.description:
The shift in mm that the import took off the coordinates of the file (the model is the file
times `unit_scale` minus `shift`).

unit_scale.description: Millimeters per unit of the file, as the import used it.

ObjectId.description: An ID: a UUID text such as 0190f1c2-7a3b-7c1d-8e2f-123456789abc.

oneOf.description: A person, in the app.
An agent, through the API.

A plug-in object that its script generated again. A Python script that calls the API is
an `Agent`.

Another user of a shared document (collaboration, PLAT-07). The editor applied their
changes with `Editor::apply_remote`.

PaintSide.description: Which side of a face a material goes on.

Resolve.description:
What to do when a component was changed by somebody else while it was open for edit
(`Command::CloseComponent`). Without an answer the close is refused.

oneOf.description:
Keep my edit as a new component (`Name#1`); the instance uses it. The other
version of the definition stays as it is.
Throw my edit away; the definition stays as it is. Works with or without a conflict.

Replace the definition with my edit, also if somebody else changed it (or if it is not
known whether they did). The other change is lost: a person says so on purpose.

ResourceBody.description: The content of a resource. `type` names it (plant_style, record_format, worksheet, hatch, tile, line_type, symbol, ... see describe: resources). The other keys depend on the type.

ResourceId.description: An ID: a UUID text such as 0190f1c2-7a3b-7c1d-8e2f-123456789abc.

SavedView.description: A saved view: name, layer visibility, active layer and camera.

items.description: A polyline point: [x, y] is a corner; {p: [x, y], kind: corner | point_on_arc | bezier | cubic} is a curved vertex; {p, kind: arc, radius} is a fillet.
A polyline point: [x, y] is a corner; {p: [x, y], kind: corner | point_on_arc | bezier | cubic} is a curved vertex; {p, kind: arc, radius} is a fillet.
A polyline point: [x, y] is a corner; {p: [x, y], kind: corner | point_on_arc | bezier | cubic} is a curved vertex; {p, kind: arc, radius} is a fillet.

anyOf.description: Structural only: the fields of these kinds are not checked.

Shape.description: A shape. `kind` names it. The kinds line, rect, circle, arc, polyline, text, plant, locus3d, polyline3d, group, landscape_area and hardscape are described field by field; the other kinds are checked for `kind` only (see describe: command_examples and the section of each feature).

SlotTarget.description: A place that takes a material: a class, an object, or a hatch.

SunSettings.description: The sun: latitude, longitude, date and time.

Transform.description: A transform of objects. Angles are radians, counterclockwise.

oneOf.description: Turn about `center`.
Scale about `center`. `sy` defaults to `sx`. A negative factor mirrors along that axis.
Mirror on the line through `a` and `b`.
Move by `delta`.

Variation.description: Random variation of placed plants: seed and ranges.

Vertex.description: A polyline point: [x, y] is a corner; {p: [x, y], kind: corner | point_on_arc | bezier | cubic} is a curved vertex; {p, kind: arc, radius} is a fillet.

VertexId.description: The id of a vertex in its surface model.

VertexKind.description: The kind of a vertex. `arc` has a radius.

ViewRules.description: Display rules: {ne_grid?: {spacing, labels?, label_height?, color?}, phases?: {enabled, existing, new, demolished}, visualization?: {name, field, rules, target?, enabled?, kinds?, include_missing?}}. See view_rules.get and the methods grid.set, phase.display and visualization.set.

oneOf.description: The 2D plan: the model point at the middle of the view and the zoom in pixels per mm.
The 3D view: an orbit camera as in the 3D window. Angles are radians, lengths are mm.

Viewpoint.description: A saved view of an issue.

classes.description: Visibility of classes when the viewpoint was made.

id.description: The ID. A nil ID in a command means "make a new one".

layers.description:
Visibility of layers when the viewpoint was made (`true`: visible). Layers that are not
listed stay as they are.

snapshot.description:
The SHA-256 of the PNG snapshot, as 64 lowercase hex digits. The file is the `image`
resource of the document with this hash (`Resources::find_image`).

time.description: When it was made, in milliseconds since 1970 (UTC).

view.description: The camera or the plan view. Without one, the viewpoint holds a selection only.

ViewpointId.description: An ID: a UUID text such as 0190f1c2-7a3b-7c1d-8e2f-123456789abc.

oneOf.description: Add an object. Missing layer or class means the active one.
Move objects. An ID that appears twice is moved once.
Change properties of one object. Missing fields stay unchanged.

Change one vertex of a polyline, landscape area or hardscape.
Missing fields stay unchanged. `kind` is a vertex kind such as
`{"kind": "arc", "radius": 50}`.

Change the record data of one object: `set` merges keys, `remove`
deletes keys. Keys in `set` are applied first.

Set or clear the import source of a layer (`provenance::LayerSource`). Importers use it for
the layers that they make.

Name the site model that the objects of a layer stand on (`site::SITE_KEY` in the data of the
layer), or clear it. Without a name an object uses the site model that covers its place.
Delete an empty layer.

Move objects in the stacking order (z-order): to the front or the back of all objects, or
one step forward or backward past the nearest object on the same layer that is not moved.

Move a layer to a place in the list of layers (0 is the first). A number past the end
puts it last.

Delete a class (a tag in the 3D modeler). The objects of the class go to `move_to` (the
default class "None", shown as Untagged, when missing). The default class cannot be deleted.
The active class becomes `move_to` when it was the deleted one.
Set or clear the georeference of the document.
Replace the display rules: the N/E grid, the phase display and the data visualization.
Set or clear the sun (heliodon) of the document.
Put a material on a slot (an object or one of its parts, a style part or a class), or clear the slot.
Choose the render style of the 3D view, or `null` for the built-in style.
Add a resource, for example a plant style. Returns its ID in `created`.
Change the name or content of a resource. Plants that use a plant style follow the change.

Delete a resource. If objects use it, the command fails unless `reassign` names
another resource of the same type that takes over.

Add one plant per position, as one step. A plant refers to `style` (if given) and
`overrides` replace style fields. Without a style the plants are by instance, with
the default style fields and the overrides.

variation.description: Random size and rotation, from a seed. Plant `i` gets the same values every time.

oneOf.description: Link plants to a style, replace their overrides, or unlink them.

Set or clear the picture of a plant style, as one step. The picture is stored once as an
`image` resource (a picture with the same hash is reused), and a picture that no style uses
any more is removed. A new picture resource is returned in `created`.

Attach a record to objects. `values` are checked against the record format. Fields
without a value get the default. Each object can have a record once.
Remove a record and its values from objects.
Change field values of a record that is attached. Other fields stay unchanged.

Add a hardscape: a slab with a `boundary`, or a path when `patch.center` gives the center line.
The patch sets the style, width, slope and so on (see `hardscape::HardscapePatch`).
Add a landscape area with a boundary, a name and settings (style, holes, drape).
Change hardscape settings of one or more hardscapes. Missing fields stay unchanged.
Change the style, holes or options of landscape areas.
Add a sheet layer with its page settings, as one step. Returns the layer ID in `created`.

Change the page of a sheet layer. Missing fields stay unchanged.
`paper` is a size id (`a3`, `letter`, ...) or `{custom: {width_mm, height_mm}}`.
Change the project data that title blocks show. Missing fields stay unchanged.
Set the stable project GUID (22 characters of the IFC base64 alphabet). IFC export sets it once.
Store a saved view. A view with the same name is replaced.

Apply a saved view: layer and class visibility and the active layer and class.
The camera part (zoom, pan, 3D view) is for the host to apply.

Place a worksheet in the drawing as a table. `at` is the top left corner and `size` the
frame in mm (paper mm on a sheet layer). The table is drawn from the calculated worksheet.
Change tables: the worksheet, the text height or the size of the frame (the top left corner stays).

Make a group of objects. They must be on one layer and in the same group (or in none).
A click on a group selects it as a whole. Returns the ID of the group in `created`.

Add an object as a member of a group (on the layer of the group). Use it when you draw inside a group
you have entered. Returns the ID of the object in `created`.

id.description:
The ID of the new object. Without one a new ID is made. A program that makes the same
objects again and again (the shapes of a plug-in object) gives IDs that follow from the
source (`Uid::derive`), so two users who do it at the same time make the same IDs. It
fails if an object with this ID exists.

oneOf.description:
Move objects into a group (`parent`) or out of all groups (no parent). The objects must be on the
layer of the group. A group that loses its last member goes.
Dissolve groups by one level: the members stay (in the group above, if any) and the group object goes.

Turn objects about a point. A group turns as one unit. Angles are radians, counterclockwise.
Hardscapes, landscape areas and site models cannot be turned.

Copy objects and move the copies by `delta`. A group is copied with its members. Returns the
IDs of the copies of `ids` in `created`, then the IDs of copied members.

Make a symbol definition from objects (groups count as their members). The insertion point is
in the drawing (default: the center of the objects). With `replace` the objects are replaced by one instance.
Returns the ID of the definition and then, with `replace`, the ID of the instance in `created`.
Replace symbol instances by groups of plain objects.

Edit the definition of a symbol in place: its 2D components become a group at the instance
(the instance is hidden meanwhile). Returns the ID of the group in `created`.
End editing in place: the objects of the edit group become the 2D components of the definition.

Set the visibility mode of layers and classes: visible, grey (drawn in grey, cannot be
picked or edited) or invisible. See `crate::visibility`.

Scale, mirror, turn or move objects (a group as one unit), in place or as copies. With
`copy` the originals stay and the copies are returned in `created`. See `edit2d::Transform`.

Add an object with a new shape that takes everything else from `source`: layer, class,
attributes, group and record data (not the transient editing keys of symbols). The edit
tools use it for the pieces they cut from an object. Returns the ID in `created`.

Duplicate array: linear, rectangular or circular copies of objects (a group as one unit).
Returns the IDs of the copies of `ids` in `created`. See `edit2d::ArrayParams`.

Move, turn or scale objects in 3D, or copy them (MOD-05; the 3D tools of the modeler). The
map `matrix` has 12 numbers (the three columns of the 3x3 part, then the translation) in
world coordinates (the `z` includes the elevation of the layer). Surface models and
component instances take any affine map through their transform (a turn about any axis,
a stretch along any axes, a shear). Plan objects (plants, hardscapes, site models, symbols,
extrudes and the like) take only maps that keep the vertical: a move (its height is
ignored, with a note: their heights come from their layer), a turn about a vertical axis,
and a scale in the plan, with the rules of `TransformObjects`. A group moves as one unit.
With `copy` the originals stay; `count` copies are made, the first placed by the map, the
next by the map applied twice, and so on (an array along a vector, or around an axis), and
their IDs are returned in `created`, copy by copy. One undo step.

Add a review issue (REV-04). A nil `issue.id` (and nil viewpoint ids) make new IDs; an ID
from a BCF file stays. `pictures` are the PNG snapshots of the viewpoints: each becomes an
`image` resource, once per hash. Returns the ID of the issue first in `created`, then those
of its viewpoints.

Change fields of an issue. Fields that are left out stay. `now` is the new change time
(milliseconds since 1970). A patch that changes nothing makes no undo step.
Delete an issue with its comments. A snapshot picture that no other viewpoint uses goes too.

Add a comment to the thread of an issue. A nil `comment.id` makes a new ID (returned in
`created`).
Change the text of a comment. `now` is the edit time.
Delete a comment.

Add a viewpoint to an issue, with its PNG snapshot if it has one. Returns the ID in
`created`.

Replace a viewpoint of an issue (the one with the same ID) with a new one, for example a
new camera or a new snapshot. A snapshot that no viewpoint uses any more goes.
Delete a viewpoint of an issue. Comments that referred to it keep their text.

Edit a surface model (MOD-06, see `crate::surface`): add edges, erase edges or faces, or
reverse faces. One undo step; an edit that fails changes nothing.

Make Group (MOD-07, see `crate::component`): the chosen faces and edges of the surface model
`model` and the chosen `objects` (groups, component instances, whole surface models) go into
a new group. The geometry moves into a surface model of its own (same ids and placement), so
it no longer welds to the rest. The objects and the model must be on one layer and in one
group. Returns the ID of the group, then the ID of the new surface model, if one was made.

Make Component: the same choice as `MakeGroup` becomes the parts of a new component
definition (a symbol), and, with `replace` (default true), one instance takes its place.
Returns the ID of the definition, then the ID of the instance.

Explode groups and component instances: their surface models merge into the surface model of
the level (the first one among the siblings, else the first one of the group becomes it),
welding and making faces by the rules of surface models; groups and instances inside move up
one level. An instance that was the last user of its definition takes the definition with it.

Make Unique: each instance gets a copy of its definition. Instances in one call that share a
definition share the copy. Fails for an instance that is the only user of its definition.

Edit Component: the parts of the definition become objects in an edit group at the instance
(the instance is hidden meanwhile). Returns the ID of the edit group.

Close Component: the objects of the edit group become the parts of the definition, and every
instance shows the change. If somebody else changed the definition while it was open, the
close is refused (a conflict) unless `resolve` says what to do: `keep_as_new` keeps this
edit as a new component for this instance, `discard` throws this edit away.

Hide (`hidden: true`) or show the objects and the members of the groups among them (MOD-05).
The mark is the data key `kadakas.hidden`, which `set_data` cannot write. A hidden object
stays in the document. Views, picking and exports leave it out.
Several commands as one undo step. Stops at the first error.
